newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat welcomes U.S. participation in meeting.
newsitem.headline: Arafat welcomes U.S. participation in meeting.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat welcomed on Thursday U.S. agreement to take part in a meeting he hopes will save Middle East peace from a crisis over Israeli settlement plans in the West Bank.
"I was waiting for this very positive stand from the American administration because they know that Israelis are breaching the agreement," Arafat told reporters in the self-ruled Gaza Strip.
Arafat has called for a meeting of U.S., European and Arab envoys in Gaza on Saturday. Washington has said it will send Edward Abington, the U.S. consul general in Jerusalem.
Netanyahu angered Palestinians and drew international condemnation with a cabinet decision this month to build 6,500 houses for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem.

Palestinians were further enraged when Israeli police issued closure orders to four Palestinian offices in East Jerusalem, saying they were run by the Palestinian Authority in violation of Israeli-PLO peace deals.
Israel vowed again on Thursday to break ground soon on the settlement but said it was reconsidering orders to close four Palestinian offices in the city.

Israel views Jerusalem as its undivided capital while the PLO regards East Jerusalem, captured by the Jewish state in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed, as the capital of a future Palestinian state.
